summary: Describes a URN namespace that OASIS uses to name persistent resources it publishes, such as OASIS standards, DTDs, schemas, and stylesheets.

plainLanguage.summary: A URN is a name for a thing that does not say where the thing lives, so it keeps working when the file moves. This memo registers one such namespace for OASIS, the standards body, and sets out the shape of the names it hands out for its specifications, committee documents and members. It also says who issues the names and how they are looked up.

questions: what is the oasis urn namespace
how does oasis name its documents
what are the branches of the oasis namespace
subtitle: A namespace for OASIS to give its published documents names that do not change when the files move.

tldr.problem: OASIS publishes specifications, drafts, schemas and stylesheets, and a name for each of them that stays the same wherever the file is hosted is worth having.
tldr.mechanism: The memo registers the URN namespace oasis for OASIS and defines the shape of its namespace specific string: a names branch with specification, tc and technical document classes, and a member branch. The Director of Technical Operations issues the identifiers.
tldr.outcome: URNs in the namespace resolve through OASIS TR9401 catalogs and, in future, an online resolution service. The memo is Informational, and the object identifiers it uses are test identifiers rather than a standard.

facts.label: Document classes in the names branch

today: RFC 3121 is an Informational memo registering a URN namespace, and the metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated. It defines a namespace for OASIS, with identifiers issued by the Director of Technical Operations and resolution through OASIS TR9401 catalogs. It is read with RFC 2141, which defines URN syntax, and RFC 2483 on the resolution services a URN needs.

sections.title: Why OASIS Wants Names That Do Not Move
sections.content:
The Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards (OASIS) produces many kinds of document: specifications, working drafts, technical resolutions, schemas and stylesheets. OASIS wishes to provide global, distributed, persistent, location-independent names for these resources.

The reason given is that the Extensible Markup Language (XML) requires all resources to provide a system identifier, which must be a URI, in addition to an optional public identifier that provides an alternate mechanism for constructing identifiers, and many evolving specifications require authors to identify documents by URI alone, among them XML Namespaces, XML Schema and XSLT. Motivated by these observations, OASIS would like to assign URNs to some resources in order to retain unique, permanent, location-independent names for them.

The namespace specification is for a formal namespace. The namespace identifier requested is oasis. The registration information gives registration version number 3 and a registration date of 2001-02-05, with Karl Best of OASIS as the declared registrant of the namespace.
sections.plainLanguage: Documents are published on the Web and later move, get revised, or are replaced. A URN is a permanent label that says which document it is without saying where to fetch it, and OASIS wanted one for everything it publishes.

sections.title: The Shape of the OASIS Namespace
sections.content:
The namespace specific string of every URN OASIS assigns has a hierarchical structure, and there are two branches at the top of the hierarchy: names and member.

The names branch begins with a document class identifier, and there are three classes. The specification hierarchy is for OASIS specifications, and the general structure of its namespace specific string is urn:oasis:names:specification:{specification-id}:{type}{:subtype}?:{document-id}, where the specification identifier is unique for the specification, the type identifies the document type such as document, schema, stylesheet, entity or xmlns, the optional subtype provides additional information about the document type, for example the stylesheet or schema language, and the document identifier is unique for the document. The tc hierarchy is for work products of OASIS Technical Committees, and has the form urn:oasis:names:tc:{tc-id}:{type}{:subtype}?:{document-id}, where the committee identifier is unique to the Technical Committee and the remaining fields are assigned as in the specification hierarchy. The technical hierarchy identifies legacy documents, namely Technical Notes, Resolutions, Memoranda and Research Papers, and has the form urn:oasis:names:technical:{document-type}:{document-id}:{amendment-id}, where the document type is one of note, resolution, memorandum or researchpaper. The document and amendment identifiers are derived from the legacy system for naming these documents: the document identifier consists of a two digit year and a sequential number, and the amendment identifier is the year of the amendment.

The members branch begins with a unique member identifier assigned by OASIS, and the string following the member identifier is opaque. The example given is urn:oasis:member:A00024:x. The member identifiers are assigned by the Director of Technical Operations at OASIS, and the opaque string is defined by the owner of the branch that begins with urn:oasis:member:{member-id}:.

On assignment and resolution, the memo says identifier uniqueness will be enforced by the Director of Technical Operations, who assigns unique identifiers to all documents identified by a URN, and that OASIS is committed to maintaining the accessibility and persistence of all the resources that are assigned URNs. Assignment is limited to the owner and those authorities specifically designated by the owner, though OASIS will assign portions of its namespace, specifically those under the members hierarchy, for assignment by other parties. For resolution, the owner will distribute catalogs, OASIS TR9401 Catalogs, that map the assigned URNs to resource identifiers such as URLs, and a more interactive, online resolution system will also be deployed in the near future; the owner will authorize additional resolution services as appropriate. URNs in this namespace are lexically equivalent if they are lexically identical, conformance with URN syntax needs no special consideration, and the validation mechanism is the published catalog, since the presence of a URN in a catalog indicates that it is valid. The scope of the namespace is global.
sections.plainLanguage: Every name starts with the same prefix and then says what kind of thing it names: an OASIS specification, a committee's working document, an older note or resolution, or a member. A single office inside OASIS hands out the numbers, and catalogs map each name to the address the document can be fetched from.

sections.title: Example URNs
sections.content:
The memo gives four examples, and says they are not guaranteed to be real and are listed for pedagogical reasons only.

  • urn:oasis:names:specification:docbook:dtd:xml:4.1.2 names a specification with the specification identifier docbook, document type dtd, subtype xml and document identifier 4.1.2.
  • urn:oasis:names:tc:docbook:dtd:xml:docbook:5.0b1 names a Technical Committee work product of the docbook committee, with document type dtd, subtype xml and document identifier docbook:5.0b1.
  • urn:oasis:names:technical:memo:9502:1995 names a legacy memorandum, with document identifier 9502 and amendment year 1995.
  • urn:oasis:member:A00024:x names a member identifier with an opaque trailing string.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show the same pieces in different orders: which kind of thing is named, which document it belongs to, and then the identifier of the document itself. The trailing part of a member name is whatever its owner wants it to be.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo says there are no additional security considerations other than those normally associated with the use and resolution of URNs in general.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing extra. The usual care needed when looking up and using a URN applies.
